title: Pricing debt as interest paid per sprint, not as a number in a spreadsheet

videos.script: Every team has a list of technical debt, and almost every list gives one number per item. How long the fix would take. {{list}} That number is the principal. It is real, and on its own it persuades nobody, because nobody is ever forced to pay it. This lesson prices debt the other way round. What does it cost every sprint that it stays where it is? That cost is the interest, and it gets paid whether anybody decides to pay it or not. {{interest}} Coreto has four debts. We measure the interest on each one, from merge times, from incident hours and from what the engineers record. {{measure}} Then you build the first sheet of the course where you compute. One division turns a principal and an interest into a payback in sprints, and the order of the four debts changes. {{sheet}} Last, the debt that grows. The seat-hold locking charges two more hours every sprint, and that brings the day it should have been paid two sprints closer. {{growth}}
